meta.title: Personal mobility devices, bicycles, mopeds and convoys
meta.summary: You will learn where cyclists, e-scooter riders and moped riders may travel and under what rules, what this means for a car driver, what rights drivers with a mobility disability have, and how to travel in a convoy in poor visibility.

lesson.h: Why a driver needs to know the rules for personal mobility devices and bicycles
p: Cyclists and e-scooter riders have no bodywork to protect them. Any mistake by a driver is more dangerous for them than for another car. If you know where they are supposed to ride and what is forbidden for them, you can anticipate where they might appear from.
Chapter 24 of the Rules sets out additional requirements for e-scooters, bicycles, small electric vehicles (hoverboards, monowheels and similar devices), horse-drawn carts and the herding of animals.

lesson.h: Cyclists: where they may ride, and from what age
p: A cyclist rides on a cycle track or cycle lane. If there is none, they ride at the right-hand edge of the carriageway (including in a lane for route vehicles) in single file, or on the shoulder, the pavement or a footpath, without endangering pedestrians ⟦16⟧.

Children under 14 must not ride a bicycle at the right-hand edge of the carriageway, in a lane for route vehicles, or on the shoulder ⟦17⟧. So a child cycling on the carriageway is a breach of the rules, but you must still be ready for it.
lesson.tip: The minimum age for cycling on the carriageway is 14; for a moped it is 16.

p: An e-scooter travels on a cycle track or cycle lane. If there is none, it travels at the right-hand edge of the carriageway (including in a lane for route vehicles) in single file, or on the shoulder ⟦18⟧.

From 25 August 2026, riding an e-scooter on pavements and footpaths is prohibited: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 326-VIII of 24.06.2026 removed this permission from the Road Traffic Act (art. 57(5)). The text of para. 168-1 still mentions the pavement (at a speed of up to 6 km/h), but the Act takes precedence, so the prohibition applies.

You may ride an e-scooter at the right-hand edge of the carriageway and in a lane for route vehicles only from the age of 18 and if you hold a driving licence of any category ⟦19⟧. On the carriageway, the helmet must be fastened ⟦20⟧.
list: Cycle track or cycle lane - first choice
No cycling infrastructure: right-hand edge of the carriageway (18+, licence, helmet) or the shoulder
Pavement and footpath - not allowed (from 25.08.2026). A cyclist without a cycle track may still use the pavement, if it does not impede pedestrians
From 1 July 2026, rental e-scooters must have registration plates and insurance
An e-scooter rider is fined for riding on the pavement as an “other road user” - 2 MCI (8 650 tenge), CAO art. 615

lesson.h: What is forbidden for cyclists and e-scooter riders
p: These prohibitions from para. 171 help a driver predict a cyclist's behaviour. For example, a cyclist must not turn left from a multi-lane road, so a sudden move to the left is a breach of the rules that you need to be ready for.
list: Riding without holding the handlebars with at least one hand
Carrying passengers (except on bicycles fitted with special equipment)
Carrying a load, except a load on bicycles fitted with special equipment and a load that projects no more than 50 cm
Turning left or making a U-turn on roads with tram traffic and on roads with more than one lane in that direction
Towing or being towed (except a bicycle trailer)
Crossing the carriageway on a pedestrian crossing while riding the vehicle: you must dismount
Riding on the carriageway during the hours of darkness without a retroreflective item
Riding on the carriageway without the helmet fastened

p: Riders of small electric vehicles (monowheels, hoverboards, segways and similar devices) are forbidden to ride on the carriageway, and to ride on the pavement or footpath if a cycle track or cycle lane is available nearby. They are also forbidden to ride without holding the handlebars (if there are any), to carry passengers or a load, to tow or be towed, or to cross the carriageway on a pedestrian crossing without getting off the device ⟦21⟧. Cycle tracks and cycle lanes are open to them: sign 4.5 permits bicycles, e-scooters and small electric vehicles.

You may ride a moped from the age of 16 ⟦22⟧. Mopeds must not use cycle tracks, cycle lanes, shoulders, pavements or footpaths (Road Traffic Act, art. 57(4)), and sign 4.5 does not permit mopeds. From 25 August 2026, bicycles with an engine are treated as mopeds (Law No. 326-VIII): they must be registered and insured, and riding one requires a category A1 driving licence (a category A or B licence also qualifies).

lesson.h: What this means for a car driver
p: On a cycle lane marked with sign 4.5 and plate 7.14, other vehicles must not drive or stop ⟦23⟧.

If this lane is separated from the rest of the carriageway by a broken line, you change lane into it before turning, giving way to cyclists riding along it ⟦24⟧. You may also move into it when entering the road, and to pick up or set down passengers at the right-hand edge ⟦25⟧.
When turning right or left, a driver gives way to cyclists who are using a cycle track to cross the road that the driver is turning into ⟦26⟧.

At an uncontrolled crossing of a cycle track with a road away from an intersection, the cyclist gives way to vehicles travelling on that road ⟦27⟧. But if the cyclist has already moved onto the road, your task is to avoid hitting them.
lesson.tip: A solid line next to a cycle lane - you must not move into it; a broken line - you may, to turn, to enter the road, or to pick up or set down passengers.

p: Convoys of cyclists on the carriageway are divided into groups of 10 cyclists (for carts, groups of 5). There is a gap of 80-100 m between groups, so that vehicles can overtake them easily ⟦28⟧.

Horse-drawn carts, riders and pack animals travel in the far right-hand lane in single file, or on the shoulder, if they do not impede pedestrians ⟦29⟧. When pulling out from a minor road at a place with poor visibility, the driver leads the animal by the bridle ⟦30⟧.

Animals are herded, as a rule, during daylight hours, close to the right-hand edge of the road ⟦31⟧. When crossing railway tracks, the herd is divided into groups ⟦32⟧. Animals must not be left unattended near paved roads, or herded outside places set aside for this ⟦33⟧.

If animals are herded in darkness, the herdsman warns drivers: standing 10-15 m from the herd, he swings a burning torch or a lantern by hand towards an approaching vehicle ⟦34⟧. If you see this signal, slow down.

Chapter 25 makes life easier for people who find it hard to walk. Signs 3.28, 3.29 and 3.30, which prohibit parking, do not apply to vehicles driven by drivers with a mobility disability, or to vehicles that serve such people or people with total loss of sight ⟦35⟧. Sign 3.27 does apply to them, but paras. 178-180 give special rights, described below. Such vehicles are fitted with suitable control mechanisms or adaptations.

Sign 5.15 with plate 7.17 “Persons with disabilities” marks a parking place only for invalid carriages and vehicles displaying the “Person with a disability” sign. Plate 7.18 “Except persons with disabilities” removes the effect of a prohibitory or mandatory sign for such vehicles ⟦36⟧.

A driver with a mobility disability, in a vehicle displaying the “Person with a disability” sign, may, in a built-up area, stop and leave the vehicle in the zone of signs prohibiting stopping or parking, if the vehicle stands entirely on the pavement and a strip at least 1.5 m wide is left for pedestrians. Where markings prohibit stopping, this does not apply ⟦37⟧. The same driver may also stay longer than the time limit in places with limited parking time, and in courtyards outside designated parking places, provided this does not obstruct anyone.

The driver of a vehicle with this sign that serves people with a mobility disability or total loss of sight may stop in the zone of signs prohibiting stopping, to pick up or set down such a person ⟦38⟧. If the driver walks the person by the hand to their destination and back, the vehicle is left on the conditions of para. 178: entirely on the pavement ⟦39⟧.

lesson.h: New Chapter 26: convoys in poor visibility
p: In fog, a blizzard or a dust storm, vehicles are sometimes driven in a convoy. Chapter 26 was added to the Rules in November 2025. Its point is that everyone drives as a single unit, behind the lead vehicle, and no one acts on their own.
list: A convoy travels in single file, as close as possible to the right-hand edge, unless it is escorted by emergency and special service vehicles ⟦40⟧
A convoy of more than 10 vehicles is escorted by at least 2 vehicles with a flashing blue, or blue and red, beacon ⟦41⟧
Speed and following distance are set by the convoy commander or the lead vehicle ⟦42⟧
A convoy without an escort is divided into groups of no more than 5 vehicles, with a distance between groups that allows overtaking ⟦43⟧
When a convoy stops on the road, everyone switches on their hazard warning lights ⟦44⟧
A member of the convoy follows the instructions of the lead vehicle and the rear vehicle, and keeps a safe following distance ⟦45⟧
You must not overtake other members of the convoy, leave the convoy, or stop without authorisation, except for a forced stop ⟦46⟧

lesson.h: How a convoy moves off and stops
p: Before moving off, everyone starts their engine and switches on dipped headlights or daytime running lights. Anyone who is not ready informs the rear vehicle. The rear vehicle blocks the lane, makes sure everything is safe, and gives permission to the lead vehicle. The lead vehicle sounds the horn and moves off ⟦47⟧.
To stop the convoy, the lead vehicle signals by braking and indicating right, reduces speed, pulls onto the shoulder and stops parallel to the road ⟦48⟧.
If you need to make an emergency stop, inform the lead vehicle by voice, by a hand signal, over the radio and (or) by flashing the main-beam headlights and sounding the horn ⟦49⟧.

When entering a parking area, a member of the convoy stops at the entrance and moves on once the vehicle ahead has finished parking ⟦50⟧. The convoy passes intersections, level crossings and traffic lights under the general rules. If a gap opens up, the rear vehicle informs the lead vehicle, who decides whether to stop or continue ⟦51⟧.

keyFacts: You may ride a moped from the age of 16 ⟦1⟧
Children under 14 must not ride a bicycle on the carriageway, in a lane for route vehicles, or on the shoulder ⟦2⟧
On the carriageway, an e-scooter may be ridden only from the age of 18, with a driving licence of any category and with the helmet fastened ⟦3⟧
From 25.08.2026, pavements and footpaths are prohibited for e-scooters (Law No. 326-VIII)
On a cycle lane (sign 4.5 with plate 7.14), other vehicles must not drive or stop ⟦4⟧
A load on a bicycle or e-scooter must not project more than 50 cm ⟦5⟧
Convoys of cyclists are divided into groups of 10, with 80-100 m between groups ⟦6⟧
At an uncontrolled crossing of a cycle track with a road away from an intersection, the cyclist gives way ⟦7⟧
A driver with a mobility disability, when leaving a vehicle on the pavement, must leave at least 1.5 m for pedestrians ⟦8⟧
A convoy of more than 10 vehicles is escorted by at least 2 vehicles with blue or blue-and-red beacons ⟦9⟧
A convoy without an escort is divided into groups of no more than 5 vehicles ⟦10⟧
When a convoy stops on the road, hazard warning lights are switched on in all vehicles ⟦11⟧
mistakes: Thinking you may ride an e-scooter on the pavement if you go no faster than 6 km/h. This rule has been repealed: from 25.08.2026, pavements and footpaths are closed to e-scooters (Law No. 326-VIII).

Thinking you may stop briefly on a cycle lane. You may not: other vehicles must not stop on a lane with sign 4.5 and plate 7.14. Moving into it is allowed only where the line is broken, and only to turn, to enter the road, or to pick up or set down passengers ⟦12⟧.
Thinking that a cyclist on a cycle track always has priority. At an uncontrolled crossing of a cycle track with a road away from an intersection, it is the cyclist who must give way ⟦13⟧.
Thinking a 12-year-old child may cycle at the edge of the road. On the carriageway and the shoulder, this is allowed only from the age of 14 ⟦14⟧.
Thinking you may overtake a slow neighbour in a convoy. Overtaking other members of the convoy is forbidden ⟦15⟧.
Thinking an e-scooter is just like a bicycle, so the pavement is allowed. A cyclist without a cycle track may use the pavement, but from 25.08.2026 e-scooters may not.

questions.q: From what age may a cyclist ride at the right-hand edge of the carriageway?
options: From the age of 12
From the age of 16
From the age of 14
From the age of 18
questions.explain: Cyclists who have not yet turned 14 must not ride at the right-hand edge of the carriageway, in a lane for route vehicles, or on the shoulder.

questions.q: September 2026. There is no cycle track nearby. A teenager on an e-scooter is riding slowly on the pavement, at about 5 km/h. Is he breaking the rules?
options: No: you may ride on the pavement if your speed is no more than 6 km/h
Yes: from 25.08.2026, pavements are prohibited for e-scooters
No, if he has a fastened helmet and a reflector
Yes, but only if pedestrians are walking on the pavement nearby
questions.explain: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 326-VIII of 24.06.2026 removed from art. 57 of the Road Traffic Act the permission to ride an e-scooter on the pavement at up to 6 km/h. From 25 August 2026, pavements and footpaths are closed to e-scooters, even though para. 168-1 of the Rules still contains this permission: the Act takes precedence.
questions.ref: Road Traffic Act, art. 57(5) (as amended by Law No. 326-VIII); para. 168-1

questions.q: There is no cycle track or cycle lane. Which of these e-scooter riders may ride at the right-hand edge of the carriageway?
options: A 25-year-old with a category B licence, helmet fastened
A 16-year-old with no licence, wearing a fastened helmet
A 30-year-old rider with a category B licence, but no helmet
A 17-year-old with no licence, but wearing a reflective vest
questions.explain: You may ride an e-scooter at the right-hand edge of the carriageway only from the age of 18 and if you hold a driving licence of any category ⟦52⟧. On the carriageway, the helmet must be fastened ⟦53⟧.

questions.q: You are riding a moped. A cycle track with sign 4.5 runs alongside the road. May you ride on it so as not to get in the way of vehicles?
options: Yes, if you ride no faster than 20 km/h and give way to cyclists
Yes, if the moped has an electric engine
Yes, but only during daylight hours and wearing a helmet
No: mopeds are forbidden to ride on a cycle track
questions.explain: Sign 4.5 permits only bicycles, e-scooters and small electric vehicles, and mopeds are not on that list. The Road Traffic Act (art. 57(4)) expressly forbids mopeds to use cycle tracks, cycle lanes, shoulders, pavements or footpaths.

questions.q: You need to set down a passenger at the right-hand edge. On the right there is a cycle lane with sign 4.5 and plate 7.14, separated by a broken line. May you move into it to set the passenger down?
options: No: stopping on a cycle lane is always prohibited
Yes: this is allowed for picking up and setting down passengers
Yes, but only during the hours of darkness, when there are no cyclists
No: you may move into it only before turning right
questions.explain: Stopping on a cycle lane is normally prohibited ⟦54⟧. But if a lane with sign 4.5 and plate 7.14 is separated by a broken line, para. 166 allows you to move into it to turn, to enter the road, or to pick up or set down passengers at the right-hand edge. You must give way to any cyclists on the lane while doing so ⟦55⟧.

questions.q: A cyclist is riding at the right-hand edge of a street that has two lanes in his direction, with no tram traffic. He needs to turn left. What should he do?
options: Dismount and cross the road on a crossing, wheeling the bicycle
Change into the left-hand lane and turn left, giving a hand signal
Turn left directly from the right-hand edge, giving way to oncoming traffic
Ride across the pedestrian crossing without getting off the bicycle
questions.explain: On roads with more than one lane for travel in a given direction, cyclists are forbidden to turn left or make a U-turn ⟦56⟧. To get to the left, a cyclist dismounts and crosses the road on a pedestrian crossing, wheeling the bicycle, that is, now as a pedestrian.

questions.q: A driver with a mobility disability, in a vehicle displaying the “Person with a disability” sign, wants to leave it on the pavement in town, in the zone of a sign prohibiting stopping. Under what condition is this allowed?
options: The vehicle stands with two wheels on the pavement, leaving pedestrians 1 m
The vehicle is entirely on the pavement, leaving pedestrians at least 0.5 m
The vehicle is at the edge of the carriageway with the hazard warning lights on
The vehicle is entirely on the pavement, leaving pedestrians at least 1.5 m
questions.explain: In a built-up area, such a driver may stop and leave the vehicle in the zone of signs prohibiting stopping or parking, if it stands entirely on the pavement and a clear strip at least 1.5 m wide is left for pedestrians. Where markings prohibit stopping, this rule does not apply.

questions.q: In heavy fog, a convoy of 9 vehicles is being formed without an escort of emergency and special service vehicles. How should it be organised?
options: All 9 vehicles travel as one group, closely following one another
Divide it into groups of 3 vehicles with a following distance of no more than 10 m
Divide it into groups of up to 5 vehicles, with a distance for overtaking
Travel in two rows, so the convoy is shorter and more visible
questions.explain: A convoy without an escort of emergency and special service vehicles is divided into groups of no more than 5 vehicles. The distance between groups must allow other vehicles to overtake them.

questions.q: A convoy in poor visibility stops right on the road. What must every member of it do?
options: Switch off all lights, so as not to dazzle oncoming drivers
Switch on the hazard warning lights
Get out and put out a warning triangle
Switch on the main-beam headlights
questions.explain: When a convoy stops on the road, the hazard warning lights are switched on in all vehicles.

questions.q: You are travelling in a convoy in a blizzard. The vehicle ahead of you is going too slowly, and you feel the convoy is falling behind. What is correct?
options: Overtake it and take a place closer to the lead vehicle
Leave the convoy and continue on your own, but carefully
Stay in your place and inform the lead vehicle of the problem
Keep sounding your horn so the driver ahead speeds up
questions.explain: In a convoy, you must not overtake other members or leave the convoy ⟦57⟧. Speed is set by the convoy commander or the lead vehicle ⟦58⟧, and members inform the lead vehicle or the rear vehicle of any circumstances hindering progress ⟦59⟧.

questions.q: There is no cycle track on the street. Riding slowly on the pavement, without impeding pedestrians, are a cyclist on a blue bicycle and a rider on a green e-scooter. Which of them is breaking the rules?
options: Only the e-scooter rider
Only the cyclist
Both the cyclist and the e-scooter rider
Neither the cyclist nor the e-scooter rider
questions.explain: If there is no cycle track, a cyclist may ride on the pavement, provided this does not endanger pedestrians ⟦60⟧. For e-scooters, this permission was withdrawn from 25.08.2026 (Law No. 326-VIII): they are left with the cycle track, the cycle lane, the right-hand edge of the carriageway, or the shoulder.
questions.ref: para. 166; Road Traffic Act, art. 57(5) (as amended by Law No. 326-VIII)

questions.q: There is no cycle track or cycle lane. Ahead, at the right-hand edge of the carriageway, a 17-year-old is riding an e-scooter, with the helmet fastened. He has no driving licence. Is he breaking the rules?
options: No: he has the helmet fastened and is riding at the right-hand edge
No, if his speed is no more than 25 km/h
Yes, but only during the hours of darkness without a reflector
Yes: on the carriageway, only from the age of 18 and with a driving licence
questions.explain: You may ride an e-scooter at the right-hand edge of the carriageway and in a lane for route vehicles only from the age of 18 and if you hold a driving licence of any category. Either way, you need to keep a safe lateral clearance.

questions.q: An adult e-scooter rider with a category B driving licence is riding at the right-hand edge of the carriageway. He is wearing a helmet, but the strap is not fastened. Is he breaking the rules?
options: Yes: on the carriageway, the helmet must be fastened
No: the helmet is on, and fastening it is not required
No, if he rides no faster than 25 km/h and in daylight
Yes, but only if he is riding during the hours of darkness
questions.explain: Riders of e-scooters and bicycles are forbidden to ride on the carriageway without the helmet fastened. An unfastened helmet will come off at the first impact.

questions.q: You have ridden up to an intersection on a bicycle. Along which path may you continue?
options: Only along A
Only along B
Along either
Along neither
questions.explain: There is tram traffic on this road, and on roads with tram traffic a cyclist must not turn left or make a U-turn. Riding straight ahead (B) is allowed. To get to the left, dismount and cross the road on a crossing, wheeling the bicycle.

questions.q: You have ridden up to an intersection on a bicycle. Along which path may you continue?
options: Only along A
Only along B
Along either
Along neither
questions.explain: Here there is one lane in each direction and no tram tracks, so a left turn is not forbidden for a cyclist. When turning, like any driver, he gives way to those he is required to give way to.

questions.q: A cycle track crosses a road away from an intersection, and there is no traffic light. Who goes first?
options: The cyclist, then you
You, then the cyclist
Whoever arrived first
questions.explain: At an uncontrolled crossing of a cycle track with a road away from an intersection, the cyclist gives way to vehicles on that road. But if he moves out onto it anyway, your task is to avoid hitting him.

questions.q: You are riding a bicycle along a cycle track towards a road. There is no intersection and no traffic light. Who goes first?
options: You, then the blue car
Whoever arrived first
The blue car, then you
questions.explain: At an uncontrolled crossing of a cycle track with a road away from an intersection, the cyclist gives way to vehicles travelling on that road. Give way to the blue car.

questions.q: A cycle track runs alongside the road on the right. You are turning right. Who goes first?
options: The cyclist, then you
You, then the cyclist
Whoever arrived first
questions.explain: When turning right or left, a driver gives way to cyclists who are using a cycle track to cross the road that the driver is turning into. The green cyclist is riding straight along the track, so he goes first.

questions.q: The right-hand lane is a cycle lane (sign 4.5 with plate 7.14), separated by a broken line. There are no cyclists on it. Both drivers are turning right. Which of them is doing so correctly?
options: Only the red car
Both
Neither
Only the blue car
questions.explain: If a cycle lane is separated by a broken line, vehicles change into it before turning. The blue car did this, while the red car is turning from the second lane, crossing the cycle lane right at the turn.

questions.q: You want to move into the cycle lane (sign 4.5 with plate 7.14, broken line) and stay there for 3-4 minutes while you check your route on your phone. May you?
options: Yes: up to 5 minutes counts as stopping, not parking
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
Yes, if there are currently no cyclists at all on the lane
No: standing on a cycle lane is prohibited
questions.explain: On a cycle lane with sign 4.5 and plate 7.14, other vehicles must not drive or stop. Where the line is broken, you may move into it only to turn, to enter the road, or to pick up or set down passengers, and you must not simply stand on it.

questions.q: You are pulling out of a yard, turning right. The far right-hand lane is a cycle lane (sign 4.5 with plate 7.14), separated by a broken line. Who goes first?
options: You, then the cyclist
The cyclist, then you
You: a cyclist on their own lane must give way to vehicles pulling out
questions.explain: When pulling out of a yard, you give way to everyone travelling on the road, including a cyclist on the cycle lane. Once he has passed, you may move into the cycle lane where the line is broken: this is allowed when entering the road.

questions.q: There is no cycle track. Two cyclists are riding on the carriageway side by side. Are they breaking the rules?
options: No: riding side by side makes them easier to see
No, if they have both already turned 14
Yes: at the right-hand edge, cyclists ride in single file
Yes, but only if they are riding in a lane for route vehicles
questions.explain: Without a cycle track or cycle lane, cyclists ride at the right-hand edge of the carriageway in single file. Riding two abreast, they take up almost the whole lane, and overtaking them is dangerous.

questions.q: Where may a 12-year-old child ride a bicycle?
options: At the right-hand edge of the carriageway, if riding in single file and wearing a helmet
On a cycle track, a cycle lane or the pavement, without impeding pedestrians
On the shoulder of a rural road, if it is wide
In a lane for route vehicles, if there are no buses
questions.explain: Before the age of 14, cyclists must not ride at the right-hand edge of the carriageway, in a lane for route vehicles, or on the shoulder. That leaves cycle tracks and cycle lanes, as well as pavements and footpaths, provided pedestrians are not impeded.

questions.q: After 25 August 2026, a 15-year-old is bought a bicycle with a petrol engine. May he ride it on the streets?
options: No: it now counts as a moped, and a moped may be ridden only from the age of 16
Yes: under the law it is still an ordinary bicycle
Yes, but only on the pavement and at no more than 6 km/h
Yes, from the age of 14, as with an ordinary bicycle, wearing a helmet
questions.explain: From 25 August 2026, Law No. 326-VIII treated bicycles with an engine as mopeds, and a moped may be ridden only from the age of 16 ⟦61⟧. Such a vehicle must also be registered and insured, a driving licence is required to ride it, and it must not be used on pavements or cycle tracks.
questions.ref: para. 165; Road Traffic Act, art. 1(41) (as amended by Law No. 326-VIII)

questions.q: From what age may a moped be ridden?
options: From the age of 14
From the age of 18
From the age of 21
From the age of 16
questions.explain: The right to ride a moped is granted to persons who have turned 16. For a bicycle on the carriageway, the threshold is 14; for an e-scooter on the carriageway, it is 18.

questions.q: A cyclist is carrying a board on the rack, projecting 70 cm to the rear. The bicycle has no special equipment for a load. Is he breaking the rules?
options: No: the board is securely tied to the rack
No, if he is carrying it during daylight hours
Yes: a load must not project more than 50 cm
Yes, but only if he is riding on the pavement among pedestrians
questions.explain: Cyclists and e-scooter riders must not carry a load, except a load on bicycles fitted with special equipment and a load that projects no more than 50 cm. A long board can strike others and gets in the way of steering.

questions.q: Which of these is allowed for a cyclist?
options: Riding without holding the handlebars
Carrying a passenger on the rack without a special seat
Towing a bicycle trailer
Towing another bicycle
questions.explain: Para. 171 forbids riding without holding the handlebars with at least one hand, carrying passengers without special equipment, and towing bicycles or being towed. An exception is made only for a trailer.

questions.q: A cyclist is riding on the pavement and wants to cross the road at this pedestrian crossing. What should he do?
options: Ride across the crossing without getting off the bicycle
Dismount and cross the road, wheeling the bicycle alongside
Ride across the crossing while sounding a signal
Ride across the road next to the crossing
questions.explain: Crossing the carriageway on a pedestrian crossing while on a bicycle or e-scooter is forbidden. By dismounting and wheeling the bicycle, a person becomes a pedestrian, and drivers must give way to them.

questions.q: You are driving at night outside a built-up area. Ahead, at the edge of the carriageway, a cyclist is riding in dark clothing, with no retroreflective items. Is he breaking the rules?
options: No: drivers with their main-beam headlights on will see him anyway
No, if he has a fastened helmet and a bell
Yes, but only if he is riding in a built-up area
Yes: riding at night without a retroreflective item is forbidden
questions.explain: Cyclists and e-scooter riders are forbidden to ride on the carriageway during the hours of darkness without a retroreflective item. Such a cyclist becomes visible only at the last moment, so reduce your speed and pass him with a wide lateral clearance.

questions.q: Which of these is forbidden for a rider of a monowheel or hoverboard?
options: Riding on the carriageway
Riding on a cycle track
Wheeling the device by hand on the pavement
Getting off the device before a crossing and crossing the road on foot
questions.explain: Riders of small electric vehicles (monowheels, hoverboards, segways) are forbidden to travel on the carriageway, to carry passengers or a load, to tow, or to cross the road at a crossing without getting off the device ⟦62⟧. They may ride on a cycle track: this is permitted by sign 4.5, and anyone wheeling the device by hand is treated as a pedestrian.

questions.q: How must a convoy of cyclists travel on the carriageway?
options: As one solid group, so that vehicles find it easier to get past
In groups of 5 cyclists, with 20 m between groups
In groups of 10 cyclists, with 80-100 m between groups
Two abreast, with no restrictions
questions.explain: Convoys of cyclists are divided into groups of 10 people, leaving 80-100 m between groups. This makes it easier for drivers to overtake the groups one at a time. Horse-drawn carts are divided into groups of 5.

questions.q: Where on the road do horse-drawn carts, riders and pack animals travel?
options: In the far right-hand lane in single file, or on the shoulder
In any lane, two abreast, if speed allows
Only on the pavement or a footpath
In the left-hand lane, so you can better see oncoming vehicles
questions.explain: Horse-drawn carts (sledges), and pack, draught and saddle animals, travel in the far right-hand lane in single file, or on the shoulder, if this does not impede pedestrians.

questions.q: The driver of a horse-drawn cart is pulling out from a minor road at a place with poor visibility of the road. What should he do?
options: Pull out quickly, so as not to hold up others
Lead the animal by the bridle
Give a voice signal and pull out
Pull out in reverse
questions.explain: When pulling onto a road from a minor road at a place with restricted view, the driver of a horse-drawn cart leads the animal by the bridle. This way he controls the animal and can see the road himself.

questions.q: Night-time. You have passed sign 1.24 “Cattle crossing”. Ahead, at the edge of the road, a person is swinging a lit lantern in circles by hand. What does this mean?
options: It is a police requirement to stop for a document check
The person is asking for a lift to the nearest village
It is a signal that the road ahead is closed for repairs and a detour is needed
There are animals nearby: reduce your speed and be ready to stop
questions.explain: When animals are being herded during the hours of darkness, the herdsman gives this signal while standing 10-15 m from the herd, facing an approaching vehicle. This means the animals are very close.

questions.q: As a general rule, how are animals herded along a road?
options: During the hours of darkness, when there is less traffic on the road
In the middle of the carriageway, so they can be seen from both sides
During daylight hours, close to the right-hand edge of the road
Only on the shoulder, against the flow of traffic
questions.explain: Animals are, as a rule, herded during daylight hours, and herdsmen keep them close to the right-hand edge of the road.

questions.q: Which of these is forbidden for herdsmen and animal owners?
options: Leaving animals unattended near a paved road
Dividing the herd into small groups when crossing railway tracks
Herding animals in daylight, keeping close to the right-hand edge of the road
Warning drivers at night by swinging a lit lantern
questions.explain: Animals must not be left unattended where they might get onto a paved road, herded across railway tracks and roads outside places set aside for this, or driven along asphalt if other routes are available ⟦63⟧. Dividing the herd into groups when crossing tracks is, on the contrary, mandatory ⟦64⟧.

questions.q: A driver with a mobility disability left a red car displaying the “Person with a disability” sign in the zone of this sign, and went away for an hour. Did he break the rules?
options: Yes: sign 3.28 applies to all vehicles with no exceptions whatsoever
Yes, if the vehicle stood here for more than 5 minutes
No, but only if the vehicle is entirely on the pavement
No: this sign does not apply to vehicles of such drivers
questions.explain: Signs 3.28, 3.29 and 3.30 do not apply to vehicles driven by drivers with a mobility disability, or to vehicles that serve such people or people with total loss of sight.

questions.q: A driver with a mobility disability left a red car displaying the “Person with a disability” sign in the zone of this sign, and went away for an hour. Did he break the rules?
options: No: prohibitory signs do not apply to vehicles of such drivers
Yes: at the edge of the carriageway, sign 3.27 applies to them too
No, if the driver was away for no more than one hour
No, if the vehicle has its hazard warning lights on
questions.explain: Signs 3.28-3.30 do not apply to such drivers, but sign 3.27 “No stopping” does apply. In its zone, in a built-up area, you may stop and stand only if the vehicle is entirely on the pavement and a strip at least 1.5 m wide is left for pedestrians ⟦65⟧.

questions.q: A driver with a mobility disability left a red car displaying the “Person with a disability” sign entirely on the pavement, leaving pedestrians 2 m. A solid yellow line is marked at the edge of the carriageway. May the vehicle stand here?
options: Yes: the vehicle is entirely on the pavement, and pedestrians are left more than 1.5 m
No: where markings prohibit stopping, this right does not apply
Yes, for no longer than 5 minutes
Yes, but only with the hazard warning lights on
questions.explain: The right to stop entirely on the pavement in the zone of prohibitory signs does not apply on sections where markings prohibit stopping. A solid yellow line at the edge of the carriageway is exactly such a marking.

questions.q: Whom does this sign with a plate not apply to?
options: A taxi with the taximeter switched on and a passenger
All passenger cars and motorcycles
Vehicles displaying the “Person with a disability” sign
Trucks while unloading
questions.explain: Plate 7.18 “Except persons with disabilities” removes the effect of a prohibitory or mandatory sign for invalid carriages and vehicles displaying the “Person with a disability” sign. Without this plate, sign 3.27 applies to them too, and it always applies to taxis.

questions.q: You are driving a car displaying the “Person with a disability” sign, and carrying a person with total loss of sight to a clinic. May you stop at the right-hand edge for him to get out?
options: Yes: this is allowed for setting down such a passenger
No: sign 3.27 applies to all vehicles without exception
Yes, but only if you move onto the pavement with all wheels
Yes, but only if the passenger is himself a driver with a disability
questions.explain: Drivers of vehicles displaying the “Person with a disability” sign, who serve people with a mobility disability or total loss of sight, may, in built-up areas, stop in the zone of signs prohibiting stopping, to pick up or set down such a person.

questions.q: A driver with a mobility disability, in a vehicle displaying the “Person with a disability” sign, left it where standing is allowed for no more than an hour, and stayed for 3 hours. Did he break the rules?
options: Yes: the parking time limit applies to everyone
No, but only if he paid for all 3 hours
Yes, if more than 2 hours have passed since the time limit ended
No: he may stand longer than the time limit, without obstructing anyone
questions.explain: Such a driver is entitled to leave a vehicle in the zone of signs prohibiting parking, at places with a limited parking time, for longer than the time limit, and in courtyards outside designated parking places, provided this does not impede pedestrians or other vehicles.

questions.q: The driver of a vehicle displaying the “Person with a disability” sign is walking a person with total loss of sight by the hand to the door of a clinic and back. How may he leave the vehicle in the zone of the “No stopping” sign?
options: Entirely on the pavement, leaving pedestrians at least 1.5 m
At the edge of the carriageway, with the hazard warning lights on
On the pedestrian crossing, as close as possible to the clinic
He may not: no one may stand in the zone of this sign
questions.explain: Such a driver stops in a built-up area on the conditions of para. 178(1): entirely on the pavement, so that a clear strip at least 1.5 m wide is left for pedestrians. Where markings prohibit stopping, this does not apply.

questions.q: What requirement do the Rules impose on a vehicle driven by a driver with a mobility disability?
options: An automatic gearbox and tinted windows
A flashing yellow beacon on the roof of the vehicle
Suitable control mechanisms and (or) adaptations
Special bodywork colouring and lettering on the doors
questions.explain: Such vehicles, as well as vehicles that serve people with a mobility disability, are fitted with control mechanisms and (or) adaptations suited to the driver or passenger.

questions.q: You are travelling in a convoy in thick fog. The lead vehicle (the white car) is braking and has switched on the right-hand direction indicator. What should you do?
options: Stay behind it in the lane: the lead vehicle is just about to overtake
Follow the lead vehicle onto the shoulder, keeping your distance
Stop wherever is convenient for you, and wait for a command
Overtake the lead vehicle and take over the head of the convoy
questions.explain: To stop the convoy, the lead vehicle signals by braking and indicating right, reduces speed, pulls onto the shoulder and stops parallel to the road. The others pull off behind it and stop, keeping their distance and the formation pattern.

questions.q: In fog, a convoy of 12 vehicles is being formed; the diagram shows part of it. How must the escort of such a convoy be organised under the Rules?
options: No escort is needed; switching on dipped headlights is enough
By one vehicle with a flashing yellow beacon at the front
By any vehicle with hazard warning lights at the back of the convoy
By at least 2 vehicles with a blue or blue-and-red beacon
questions.explain: A convoy of more than 10 vehicles is escorted by at least 2 vehicles with a flashing blue, or blue and red, beacon switched on: the lead vehicle and the rear vehicle. Without such an escort, the convoy is divided into groups of no more than 5 vehicles.

questions.q: A convoy in poor visibility is preparing to move off, and your engine will not start. What should you do?
options: Wait quietly for it to start
Leave the convoy and drive on your own later
Inform the rear vehicle of the convoy
Sound your horn at the lead vehicle so the convoy leaves without you
questions.explain: Before moving off, all members start their engines and switch on dipped headlights or daytime running lights. Anyone who is not ready informs the rear vehicle, which gives the lead vehicle permission to move off.

questions.q: Who gives the lead vehicle permission to start the convoy moving?
options: Any member of the convoy, by sounding a horn
The rear vehicle, having made sure it is safe to move off
The driver of the first vehicle behind the lead vehicle, by flashing the headlights
No one: the lead vehicle moves off whenever it sees fit
questions.explain: The rear vehicle blocks the lane that the convoy is pulling into, makes sure nothing is in the way, and gives permission to the lead vehicle. The lead vehicle sounds the horn and moves off, with the others following. The rear vehicle joins in once the last member has pulled out.

questions.q: You are travelling in a convoy in a blizzard, and you urgently need to make an emergency stop. What should you do?
options: Notify the lead vehicle and smoothly reduce speed to a stop
Brake sharply and stop immediately at the point of the breakdown
Quietly pull onto the shoulder, so as not to distract the convoy
Overtake the lead vehicle and stop the whole convoy yourself
questions.explain: A member of the convoy first notifies the lead vehicle of the need for an emergency stop: by voice, by a hand signal, over the radio and (or) with the main-beam headlights and the horn. After that, he gradually reduces speed to a full stop.

questions.q: A convoy in poor visibility is passing through a controlled intersection. Two vehicles ahead of you went through on green, and the light has turned red in front of you. What should you do?
options: Go through on red, so the convoy does not split up
Go through, with the hazard warning lights and headlights on
Go through, if the lead vehicle is already on the far side of the intersection
Stop: the traffic light applies to the convoy too
questions.explain: The convoy passes intersections, level crossings and traffic lights in accordance with the general requirements of the Rules. If the convoy is split, the rear vehicle warns the lead vehicle, and the lead vehicle decides whether to stop or continue, and informs the rear vehicle of this.

questions.q: The convoy is pulling into a parking area. The vehicle ahead of you is parking. What should you do?
options: Stop at the entrance until the vehicle ahead has finished parking
Drive around it and take a free space first
Sound your horn so the driver ahead parks more quickly
Stop on the carriageway next to the parking area and wait
questions.explain: When entering a parking area, a member of the convoy stops at the entrance and resumes moving once the vehicle ahead has finished parking. This way the convoy avoids causing a traffic jam or collisions.

questions.q: You are travelling in a convoy. The rear vehicle asks you over the radio to increase the distance to the vehicle ahead. What should you do?
options: Not comply: only the lead vehicle gives commands in a convoy
Comply, but only if the lead vehicle confirms this request
Comply: the rear vehicle's instructions are binding
Overtake the vehicle ahead, so the gap appears behind you
questions.explain: A member of the convoy follows the instructions of both the lead vehicle and the rear vehicle, and keeps a safe following distance. Overtaking other members of the convoy is forbidden.

questions.q: You are about to turn right. The far right-hand lane is a cycle lane (sign 4.5 with plate 7.14, broken line), and a cyclist is riding along it. Who goes first?
options: You, then the cyclist
The cyclist, then you
You: the cyclist must give way to those who are turning
questions.explain: Before turning, you must change into the cycle lane ⟦66⟧, and when changing lane you give way to those travelling in the same direction without changing direction ⟦67⟧. Give way to the cyclist, then change lane and turn.
